title: 8K quiz (25 marks) and mark scheme
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Metals and their uses (8G); energy transfers (8K)
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 57 (8K quiz (25 marks) and mark scheme (portal))
intro: Test. Answer every question in the spaces provided. Show your working: marks are given for method. The marks for each question are shown in brackets.

questions.q: Aluminium is used for aircraft mainly because it is...
questions.a: B) Low density and resists corrosion. Planes must be light and must not corrode.
C) Nail in a dry jar. Without water, iron cannot rust.

questions.q: Why does galvanised iron not rust even when scratched?
options: Zinc is more reactive and corrodes first
questions.a: B) Zinc is more reactive and corrodes first. Zinc gives sacrificial protection.

questions.q: Which metal reacts most vigorously with cold water?
questions.a: B) Potassium. Potassium is the most reactive of these.
B) Zinc sulfate + hydrogen. Sulfuric acid makes sulfates; metals with acid give hydrogen.

questions.q: Which metal would react fastest with dilute acid?
questions.a: B) Magnesium. Magnesium is highest of the three.

questions.q: Use the data table on the sheet (density, strength, conductivity, cost, corrosion) to choose a metal for four jobs and justify each.
questions.a: Sensible choices with data, e.g. bike frame: aluminium (light, strong enough, no rust)
questions.model: Teacher does the first: 'electrical wire: copper, because the table shows the highest conductivity at a reasonable cost'.

questions.q: Explain why gold is used in phones even though it is expensive.
questions.a: Excellent conductor, does not corrode; only tiny amounts needed

questions.q: Suggest why titanium is used for hip replacements.
questions.a: Strong, low density, does not corrode or react in the body

questions.q: Why are saucepan bases often copper?
questions.a: Copper is an excellent thermal conductor, so heat spreads quickly
questions.model: What does a pan base need to do? Pass heat from the hob to the food. Which property? Good thermal conductor. Copper is one of the best.

questions.q: Which property lets copper be made into wires?
Why are overhead power cables aluminium, not copper?
questions.a: Aluminium is much less dense (lighter) and cheaper

questions.q: Set up the three-jar rust test with an adult. Write the variables and a prediction, and draw day 0.
questions.a: Variables: change conditions, observe rust, control nail type and jar; prediction with reason
questions.model: Teacher sets up jar A on camera and labels it 'tap water: air and water'.

questions.q: Why must the nails be the same size and type?
questions.a: So only the conditions change, to keep the test fair

questions.q: How could you make a jar with water but almost no oxygen? (adult method)
questions.a: Boil water to remove air, cool, add the nail and a layer of oil on top

questions.q: A bike left outside in winter rusts faster near salted roads. Explain.
questions.a: It has water and oxygen, and salt speeds up rusting
questions.model: List the conditions: rain gives water, air gives oxygen. Salt from gritted roads speeds up rusting. All three are present.
